votes.evidence: The human-authored draft case is reachable through the current hosted caller. /tmp/frozen-75215/products/tasks/backend/presentation/views/api.py:1101-1118 permits a task controller with task:write to set run output. /tmp/frozen-75215/products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:1770-1787 protects only pr_merged and explicitly permits retargeting pr_url; :2147-2154 saves it. For an existing non-internal signal-report task with an opted-in acting reviewer, /tmp/frozen-75215/products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:92-114,126-138 forwards that URL. The initial task checks a configured repository, open state and head but not author identity at /tmp/frozen-75215/products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1130-1174, then stamps inbox_review at :1176-1181,1223-1229. /tmp/frozen-75215/products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451 passes self_driving_review=True, /tmp/frozen-75215/tools/pr-approval-agent/review_local.py:321-326 accepts the human PR, and /tmp/frozen-75215/tools/pr-approval-agent/review_pr.py:590-591 waives its normal draft prerequisite. The trusted prompt incorrectly identifies it as a machine-created implementation PR at /tmp/frozen-75215/tools/pr-approval-agent/reviewer.py:695-700. This can admit an unrelated human draft, including one whose author would fail the normal hosted prefilters.
votes.refutation: My original refutation established that the Action never enables the flag, the webhook carve-out checks bots, and signal task execution forces bot authorship. Its missing premise was that output.pr_url must be the URL created by that execution. The existing set_output endpoint disproves this: the task controller can replace the URL independently, and the initial receiver/task trusts it. Thus creation-time bot authorship does not guarantee the fetched PR's author, and the webhook checks do not protect the separate initial path. The finding's ready-PR argument remains incorrect: later reviews after marking a legitimate linked PR ready are intentional (tasks.py:160-169). I keep the finding for the independently reachable human-draft gate bypass, not for requiring every later review to remain draft.

votes.evidence: A reachable human-draft path exists: products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:64-78 matches a TaskRun by branch and repository, and :178-185 records a PR from that native branch without checking the PR author; :291-292 saves output and fires receivers. Thus a human opening a draft from a signals task's pushed branch while output.pr_url is unset can enter products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:92-105,126-138, which checks the signal task and opt-in but not PR authorship. products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1159-1181,1223-1229 fetches that PR and stamps inbox provenance after checking only open state and head SHA. products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451 converts that provenance to self_driving_review; tools/pr-approval-agent/review_local.py:321-330 and review_pr.py:590 then allow the human draft through prerequisites. reviewer.py:695-700 also incorrectly calls its author a machine user. This is narrower than the reported blanket must-fix: it requires a matching signal-task branch and an opted-in reviewer.
votes.refutation: I first checked existing guards and tests. products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:168-175 rejects human authors on the webhook re-review carve-out, and products/tasks/backend/temporal/process_task/utils.py:1068-1074 forces bot credentials for signal-generated PRs. Tests in products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_tasks.py:830-887 cover fork/team/toggle/task-linkage rejection, while tools/pr-approval-agent/test_review_pr.py:569-606 preserves ordinary draft refusal and changes-requested blocking. These guards do not cover the initial receiver path: the task webhook's branch-based PR backstop accepts a human-created native-branch PR and triggers that separate path. I reject the ready-state half: tasks.py:160-163 explicitly retains draft-time approval when ready, and later head-changing re-reviews remain eligible, so demanding draft=True would break intended behavior. The human-draft path survives the refutation and is a real narrow correctness defect.

votes.evidence: The human-authored trigger is reachable in the hosted production path. products/tasks/backend/presentation/views/api.py:1082-1087 accepts an authorized task-run PATCH; presentation/serializers.py:179 accepts arbitrary output JSON. products/tasks/backend/visibility.py:22-24,30-46 permits team members to control SIGNAL_REPORT tasks. products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:1770-1788 protects only pr_merged, and :2038-2044,2075 saves caller-supplied pr_url. With an assigned reviewer opted into Stamphog, products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:92-105,111-138 dispatches that URL from a non-internal signal task. products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1140-1174 resolves an enabled GitHub repository and checks only open state/nonempty head before stamping inbox_review at :1176-1181,1223-1229; it does not verify the fetched author's type or task linkage. temporal/activities.py:434-451 turns that provenance into self_driving_review=True. tools/pr-approval-agent/review_local.py:321-324 accepts it, review_pr.py:590 skips the draft prerequisite, and reviewer.py:695-700 asserts machine provenance. Thus a task controller can point the run at an unrelated human-authored draft in an enabled repository and have it reviewed despite the ordinary draft/author trust gates; an APPROVE result is posted at temporal/activities.py:723-745. No malformed context or direct Pipeline invocation is required.
votes.refutation: I first checked whether production callers guarantee the claimed invariants. tools/pr-approval-agent/review_pr.py:196-209 defaults the flag off; products/tasks/backend/temporal/process_task/utils.py:1067-1074 forces genuine signal executions to BOT authorship; products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:169-200 rejects human/fork PRs and verifies task linkage on webhook re-reviews. These guards refute an ordinary direct-Action bypass but do not cover the initial receiver path, whose target remains caller-writable through the PATCH above. The ready-PR portion is separately refuted: tasks.py:160-165 deliberately preserves the draft-time approval when a PR becomes ready, and later head-changing re-reviews do not require draft=True. Requiring every self-driving review to remain draft would break that lifecycle. The finding survives specifically because a human-authored PR can receive the flag through the initial hosted path.
